analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Vision is a fast-growing regional consumer electronics retailer in Bihar/Eastern India with strong ROCE, but it trades at an absurd 61x earnings, carries unacceptable debt (D/E 0.65), and is burning cash at an accelerating rate — a combination that fails my most fundamental filters. This is a growth story priced for perfection in a thin-margin, disruption-prone business, which is exactly the kind of speculation I avoid.
key_strengths: Strong revenue and profit CAGR (36-44% over 3 years), showing genuine execution in an underpenetrated market
ROCE of 29.95% is impressive for a retailer, indicating decent capital efficiency on existing stores
Dominant regional positioning in Bihar/Eastern India, a low-penetration market with rising consumer aspirations
key_risks: Operating cash flow has collapsed from +32 Cr (2022) to -41 Cr (2025) — the business burns more cash every year despite reporting profits, a serious working capital problem
Debt has nearly doubled from 282 Cr to 480 Cr in 3 years, with D/E at 0.65 — far above my hard limit of 0.3
Consumer electronics retail faces existential e-commerce disruption from Amazon/Flipkart/Reliance, compressing already razor-thin 6.57% operating margins
red_flags: Free cash flow deeply negative at -78 Cr in FY25 and worsening each year — profits are not translating to cash
Promoter holding at 47.14% is below my 55% floor — insufficient skin in the game
P/E of 61x for a single-digit margin retailer is speculative, not value investing
Growth is being funded entirely by debt and equity raises (financing CF +94 Cr in FY25), not internal accruals
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aditya Vision fails my checklist at every critical junction. The cash flow story is damning: a retailer reporting INR 106 Cr net profit while burning INR 41 Cr in operating cash means inventory and receivables are growing faster than the business can collect — a classic sign of aggressive, working-capital-hungry expansion. I built DMart on exactly the opposite principle: collect cash before you pay suppliers, never the reverse. When OCF is positive in only 2 of the last 4 years and deteriorating, I worry the profit is an accounting artifact, not real money in the bank. The debt trajectory (282 → 418 → 319 → 480 Cr) tells me this company cannot self-fund its growth.

The valuation at 61x P/E for a 6.57% operating margin retailer is simply irrational by any standard I apply. Even at the forward P/E of 41x, you are paying a premium that requires flawless execution for a decade — in a sector facing relentless pricing pressure from online platforms and large-format competitors like Croma and Reliance Digital. The promoter holding below 55% adds to my discomfort. There is real underlying business here — ROCE of 30% and strong regional brand — but it must prove cash generation before warranting any serious consideration. At the right price (12-15x earnings) with a fortress balance sheet, this would be an interesting regional retail story. Today, it is not that.
